newsitem.title: FRANCE: Beaujolais nouveau 1996 air shipments increase.
newsitem.headline: Beaujolais nouveau 1996 air shipments increase.

text.p: The Beaujolais wine growers association, the UIVB, said provisional estimates indicated a growth in demand for its popular "nouveau" wine from major export markets this year compared to 1995.

"It's difficult at this stage, to give precise figures, but feedback from forwarders suggests an increase in demand from North America while the Japanese market shows signs of recovery after a slump in shipments last year largely as a result of protests about French nuclear testing in the Pacfic," a UIVB official told Reuters.
In 1995, around 4,000 tonnes of Beaujolais nouveau was transported by air, representing 60 percent of global shipments to overseas markets (excluding Europe), UIVB figures showed.
The 1996 harvest has produced a Beaujolais nouveau with a "refreshing and lively taste" and "red fruit perfume."

The fine-tuned logistics operation to ensure the wine reaches consumers worldwide in time for traditional cork-popping day, on the third Thursday in November, will be set in motion at 22.00 French time (21.00 GMT) this evening.
Air France Cargo said it would be shipping around 1,200 tonnes of Beaujolais nouveau this year compared to a total of 870 tonnes in 1995.

Apart from the well-established destinations such as New York, Chicago, Miami and Tokyo, the French state airline will be flying shipments in for the first time to Antigua, Damascus, Hanoi, Ho Chi Minh City and Maputo.
"The increase in our volume of shipments is largely due to stronger demand from the U.S and Canada and Japan," an Air France Cargo official told Reuters.

In terms of the major markets for Beaujolais nouveau, Air France will be shipping around 800 tonnes to the U.S. compared to 500 tonnes in 1995, 100 tonnes to Canada, an increase of 30 tonnes and 200 tonnes to Japan, up 60 to 70 tonnes on last year, the official said.

Apart from transporting the Beaujolais nouveau aboard scheduled cargo and passenger flights, Air France is putting on seven Beajoulais-dedicated Boeing 747-200 freighter flights over a three-day period compared to five last year.
Two of the all-cargo flights will fly from Lyon-Satolas to New York and Tokyo the first just after midnight on November 16.
The five other flights will operate from Paris/Charles-de-Gaulle with three flights to New York, one to Miami and one to Tokyo, in joint-venture with Japan Airlines .
JAL is operating an extra freighter flight Saturday November 16 carrying 87 tonnes of the wine and will also use scheduled cargo and passenger flights for shipments.
"We expect to be transporting about 240 tonnes in total compared to around 90 tonnes in 1995 which was a poor year for us in terms of Beaujolais shipments," a JAL cargo official said.
Federal Express said it planned to operate a special McDonnell Douglas MD11 "Beaujolais charter" on Saturday between CDG and Narita carrying an 87-tonne consignment.
Last year, the Memphis-based operator laid on a dedicated Boeing 747F on the same route.
Just over 30 tonnes will be shipped on its scheduled ex-Paris freighter services, a FedEx official added.

Given the fact that cargo capacity is tight at this time of the year and some airlines are putting on dedicated freighter operations, they can command rates for Beaujolais above the normal levels," an industry source told Reuters.

"For example, top rates for ex-France-Tokyo wil be between 17 and 18 (French) francs per kilo compared to standard rates for week-in-week out cargo of 15 and 16 francs." -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
